budget.THE_HEADLINE_FINDING: THE 25MB BUDGET MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THEY DIFFER BY 2 MB. `npm run build` copies frontend/public/** off DISK, so a LOCAL build measures the WORKING TREE. CI checks out the committed tree, so a CI run measures what a deploy from main actually ships. With 30 uncommitted theme rasters in the tree those are different builds.

NO SLOT, AND THE ONE REAL SLOT IS BETTER FILLED TODAY. Measured live: the celebration banner .c1-win is FULL STAGE WIDTH (1280 px, heights 111/140/172 by tier), not the narrow plate the 'compact' framing assumes. Its raster consumers are exactly three: c1-tier-burst (from ui/win/*), c1-shockwave and c1-coin (both reusing the PARTICLE files). The 256x256 centre-blooms DO have a slot (c1-tier-burst) and are measurably weaker there: energy at the real draw size is 21.56 against the incumbent bloom_mega's 42.23 and 24.71 against burst_epic's 70.77, and at 256px source against a 430-540px draw they would upscale on all three tiers where the incumbents are 665-819px. On big alone the candidate is punchier (26.70 vs 19.00) but would still upscale. Also: the whole set is 585,411 B against 339,229 of headroom, so it could not ship entire in any case.

ALL FOUR LIVE TARGETS ARE THE OWNER'S UNCOMMITTED WORK, AND THE CANDIDATES DO NOT BEAT IT. ui/particles/{spark,coin,shock_ring,smoke_puff}.png are all ' M' in the working tree, so installing candidates over them destroys owner work that is not in git. Measured at the size each is actually DRAWN, the case is weak anyway: spark draws at 22x22 from a 32px source (already oversampled), and the candidate is only +25% energy over the owner's WIP. coin draws at a randomised 16-30px from 40px (downscaled) and the candidate is SLIGHTLY WORSE than the owner's WIP (103.25 vs 108.85). shock_ring is the ONE genuinely upscaled sprite, drawn at 440-704px from 128px (3.4x to 5.5x), so resolution there would really help - but the candidate cyan-ring also tops out at 128px, giving no resolution gain, and it is 72% FAINTER (energy 10.52 against the owner's WIP 37.60, coverage 8.0% against 23.6%), which is exactly the faint filler the brief says to refuse. shock-bloom is a bright blue bloom mapped onto smoke_puff, a half-opacity deliberate blur: a different thing, not a replacement.

animation_residual_WS7.question: does the punch transform now make the 16-frame win look drunk?
animation_residual_WS7.answer: NO. It was left exactly as it is.
animation_residual_WS7.method: 31 composed captures of the hero over the 1500ms reaction, identical fixed clip, once with .hero-body[data-motion='win'] animating and once with it forced to none.
animation_residual_WS7.reading: R122 diagnosed two motions FIGHTING as excursion rising while per-sample change FALLS. Here per-step change RISES 42.3% with the punch on, and spikiness FALLS (3.54 against 4.23). The punch adds motion on top of the frames rather than cancelling them, and it fills the still moments between discrete flipbook steps: with the punch off, 8 of 30 sampled steps show almost no change at all (0.03) because the sample lands inside a held frame; with it on, none do. The win punch is translation-led and the flipbook's motion is the arms, so they are on different axes - unlike R122's idle case where two LATERAL motions fought.
animation_residual_WS7.instrument_error_corrected: the first pass of this measurement returned 0.00 for every metric and an authoritative-sounding conclusion. The captures were fine (31 distinct files) and the stepping worked; the ANALYSIS was broken - omitBackground did not yield transparency because the stage behind the hero is opaque, so alpha covered 100% of the clip and every silhouette mask was all-true. Re-run on RGB with a control that a frame differs from itself by 0 and from its neighbour by more than 0. Third instrument failure of this class in three sessions.
